note: One of six property tax notices added 2026-08-27 to give the `propertytax` sub_bill_type (commercial-narrative-v11) real coverage across municipalities -- before them the corpus held no tax notice at all, while that family accounted for 21 of the 26 misrouted payables in the B2 audit. sub_bill_type 'propertytax' is the assertion these documents exist for: measured 6/6 on a scratch analyzer, both twins agreeing at 0.858-0.892, with controls held (burnaby_water->water, business_license->business_license, bchydro->electric). City of Vancouver 2026 PROPERTY TAX NOTICE (a different parcel from property_north_van, which despite its name is also Vancouver). total 1,857.95 is the taxes due after the home owner grant; the page also prints a larger pre-grant figure. invoice_date from 'Statement Date: May 05, 2026', payment_due_date from 'Due Date: July 3, 2026'. vendor_name is upper-case 'CITY OF VANCOUVER' here and title-case on other municipal documents -- the known casing inconsistency (open-defects B6a), asserted as observed. || invoice_description NOT asserted: free-text summary that rewords every run ('Annual property tax charges for 2026.' vs '2026 property tax notice.'), excluded by the standing rule already recorded on recommend_240124_0001. It was asserted in error when this sidecar was scaffolded from only 3 replicates, all of which happened to agree. || vendor_name IS asserted. The twins return the correct municipality on every read but flip between title case and upper case ('CITY OF VANCOUVER' / 'City of Vancouver'); regress.py compares vendor_name case-insensitively (and suffix-insensitively) for exactly this reason, so the assertion still catches a WRONG vendor while ignoring a difference the pipeline does not promise. The casing itself is open-defects B6a, owned by dataverse-todo DV-4. vendor_name is base-critical and is never dropped from a sidecar. || folio_number ADDED 2026-09-09 with the new folio twins (commercial-narrative-v20). It is a critical field on property tax notices only (field_policy.PROPERTYTAX_DELTA), and is asserted on every sidecar -- the value on a tax notice, "" everywhere else -- so a regression that starts populating it on ordinary invoices is caught. || number_of_days ASSERTION REMOVED 2026-09-09 (user authorised, all 20 property_* sidecars): the Power Automate flow does not consume number_of_days for property tax. It was removed from the whole family rather than only where it flakes, so the tax notices stay uniform. Behaviour seen: the period resolves 2026-01-01..2026-12-31 on every read (365 days inclusive), number_of_days_extract returns no value at all, and number_of_days_generate intermittently invents '1' -- catalogued defect B3 -- which reconcile_number_of_days then corrects to 365, while an empty twin pair stays blank by that function's explicit 'corrects only; never supplies' design. The field therefore flipped '' <-> 365 between runs. || billing_period_start_date AND billing_period_end_date ASSERTIONS REMOVED 2026-09-09 (user authorised, all 20 propertytax sidecars): the Power Automate flow does not consume the billing period for property tax, so the corpus no longer asserts it on this family. Both fields REMAIN in WRITE_FIELDS and still reach Dynamics -- removing the assertion stops the corpus checking them, it does not stop them being written. What this gives up, stated once: on the 16 notices that asserted '' the pair was the guard against a generate twin inventing a period out of nothing, and on property_surrey it was catching a real failure chain -- B3's invented number_of_days=1 makes the code derive start = end - 1 day, which collapses the period to zero length and blanks a correct 2026-01-01 (open-defects A13b, measured 4 of 6 reads correct). That chain is unfixed and is now invisible to the corpus on every property tax notice.
